name: @w6w-apps/givebutter
description: Manage Givebutter campaigns, contacts, transactions, funds, households and webhooks — the nonprofit fundraising and donor-CRM platform.

w6w.longDescription:
Givebutter is a nonprofit fundraising platform: campaigns (donation pages, peer-to-peer, ticketed events), the transactions and recurring plans they collect, and the contacts (donor CRM) and households behind them. This app covers that core surface end to end — full CRUD on campaigns, contacts (including tag management), funds and webhooks; creating and updating transactions for offline/manual gift entry; and read access to the resources the API exposes read-only: payouts, pledges, recurring plans, tickets and outbound messages.

Givebutter's own API reference disagrees with the API's actual wire behavior in two ways this app works around rather than repeats: every documented error response is shown as a flat `{"message": ...}` object, but a live 401 actually answers `{"error": {"message": "Unauthorized"}}` — this app's error formatter reads both shapes. And the Rate Limits page states 500 requests/minute, but every live response measured during development carried `x-ratelimit-limit: 200` — the quota health check reports the header, not the doc.

One more thing worth knowing before scripting against resource paths directly: `{campaign}` and `{fund}` path parameters accept only the numeric id. A slug or any other non-numeric value in that position doesn't reach the API layer at all — it falls through to Givebutter's public marketing site, which answers its own branded 404 HTML page instead of a JSON error. This app's actions always take the numeric id.
